group.passage:
Every driver is familiar with the dreaded blind spots caused by the thick A-pillars, or the windshield frame, of a car. While these pillars hold the front and side windows of a car in place, they block a driver’s view, and might result in serious property damage or even deaths. According to the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, over 840,000 car accidents occur due to blind spots. While drivers can take precautions such as adjusting the driver’s seat and side mirrors properly, installing backup cameras and so on, they won’t eliminate the blind spots completely. Luckily, a 14-year-old girl, who doesn’t even have a driver’s license yet, has conceived of a brilliant idea.
Alaina Gassler, who often saw her mother getting frustrated by blind spots on the family’s jeep as they drove around their neighborhood, worked on a project called “Improving Automobile Safety by Removing Blind Spots.” It works in a relatively simple way. She installed an outward-facing camera onto the pillar of the car. The camera is connected to a projector, which subsequently displays a live video feed of road activities onto the interior side of the pillar. This part of the pillar is the most dangerous blind spot of the car, as it is the point furthest away from the driver. The images projected onto the pillar blend in with the actual background outside the car, essentially making a section of the car’s thick frame transparent.
For her invention, Aliana won the top prize of US$25,000 at a major science competition. She will use the money to improve her invention with LCD technology, which will put a TV-like image on the A-pillar instead of a projected image. Her next step will be getting a major car manufacturer to use the system.

figures.description: 一輛四門轎車的深色側面剪影（車頭朝左），上方三個箭頭分別標示車頂支柱：最左的「A-Pillar」指向前擋風玻璃與前車門車窗之間、由引擎蓋往車頂斜上的支柱；中間的「B-Pillar」指向前、後車門車窗之間的直立支柱；最右的「C-Pillar」指向後車窗與後擋風玻璃之間、往車尾斜下的支柱。圖示說明文中 A-pillar 的位置（即前擋風玻璃兩側的框架，文中亦以 the windshield frame 說明）。

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the first paragraph?

options.B: To tear down a widely-held myth.
options.C: To raise people’s awareness of a problem.
options.D: To cite some statistics and prove a theory.

questions.stem: Which of the following accidents is most likely the result of an A-pillar blind spot?

options.A: A car hits a motorcyclist who runs a red light.
options.B: A car crashes straight into a building on a foggy day.
options.C: A car hits a pedestrian when turning right at an intersection.
options.D: A car crashes into the back of another car at the traffic light.

questions.stem: Why should Alaina Gassler’s invention be used in a car?

options.A: It records road accidents involving the car.
options.B: It provides the driver with a full view of the road.
options.C: It turns the windshield frame into transparent glass.
options.D: It makes a car more visible to other cars on the road.

questions.stem: Which of the following CANNOT be inferred from the passage?

options.A: Alaina hopes that her invention will be mass produced.
options.B: Alaina will try to improve the image quality of her invention.
options.C: Adjusting side mirrors properly can help prevent road accidents.
options.D: Alaina’s mother often got into car accidents caused by blind spots.

tags.topic: a teenager's invention to remove car A-pillar blind spots
